facts.value: Composite not reported; sections 740-770 EBRW, 770-800 Math (enrolled Fall 2025, CDS C9)
Test-required: SAT or ACT (hardship waiver available). Score Choice allowed; SAT superscored. Latest SAT Nov 7 / ACT Oct 17, 2026 for ED; Dec 5 / Dec 12 for RD
Meets 100% of demonstrated need with grant-based, no-loan aid; need-blind for U.S., Canadian and Mexican citizens/residents. Under $200K: at least full tuition; under $75K: all billed costs
CSS Profile + FAFSA required; deadlines for an award with the admission decision: Nov 6, 2026 (ED), Feb 5, 2027 (RD)
No merit aid: all Penn financial aid awards are need-based
$99,082 COA 2026-27 on campus (tuition $65,670; fees $8,308; housing $13,644; food $6,960; books $1,412; transport $1,080; personal $2,008)
Early Decision (binding) due Nov 1, decisions in December; Regular Decision due Jan 5, decisions in April. No EA

No interviews: Penn discontinued its optional alumni interview starting with the 2025-26 cycle (per The Daily Pennsylvanian, Aug 2026). Penn's old Alumni Conversations page now redirects to a page that doesn't mention interviews; CDS 2025-26 C7 rates interview 'Not Considered'
Not considered (CDS 2025-26 C7 'Level of applicant's interest')
Apply to one of four undergraduate schools (College of Arts & Sciences, Wharton, Engineering, Nursing) or a coordinated dual-degree/specialized program (e.g. Huntsman, LSM), each with its own essay
Coordinated dual-degree and specialized programs (Huntsman, LSM and others) have extra program essays listed on the writing page, beyond the prompts recorded here

deadlines.note: Binding; decisions in December. Aid documents by Nov 6
Decisions in April. Aid documents by Feb 5

supplements.label: Thank-you note
supplements.prompt: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!) (50-200 words)

supplements.label: Community at Penn
supplements.prompt: How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn. (50-200 words)

supplements.label: Required for your school only: Nursing
supplements.prompt: Penn Nursing intends to meet the health needs of society in a global and multicultural world by preparing its students to impact healthcare by advancing science. Why are you applying to Nursing, where do you see yourself professionally in the future, and how will you contribute to our mission of promoting equity in healthcare? (50-200 words)

supplements.label: Required for your school only: College of Arts and Sciences
supplements.prompt: The College of Arts and Sciences is designed to foster discovery and connection. Describe something you are curious about—something you'd like to learn more about or find a new approach to—and how you might pursue that curiosity in the College. (50 to 200 words)

supplements.label: Required for your school only: Wharton
supplements.prompt: Wharton prepares its students to make an impact by applying business methods and economic theory to real-world problems, including economic, political, and social issues. Discuss a current issue of importance to you and how you hope a Wharton education would help you explore it. (50-200 words)

supplements.label: Required for your school only: Engineering
supplements.prompt: Penn Engineering prepares its students to become leaders in technology by combining a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics with depth of study in focused disciplinary majors. Describe how you plan to pursue your engineering interests at Penn, particularly within the intended major you selected. (50-200 words)
